scenario.title: Doctrine: Grace and Matter
scenario.premise: Across eight desks, build and question arguments about evil, freedom, bodies and grace. Manuscripts answer other manuscripts; agreement is not the same as victory. A completed argument reconstructs its author’s position, not a proof of belief.

stage.title: What can reason contribute?
stage.speaker: Aquinas’s disputation desk · thirteenth century
stage.motivation: A student asks why revelation is needed if philosophy already studies God. Meanwhile, the earlier argument for opposed origins faces a physical example and a rival reading of the good tree. Try Aquinas’s answers without treating the questions as settled.

objectives.text: Answer why revelation is needed alongside philosophy
Test opposed origins against Aquinas’s fire example
Compare the rival readings of the good tree

things.label: Two Principles versus Augustine: opposed source or damaged good?
